comparison: Both evaluate the DUF regulatory function and UMP inhibition data (C116, C117, C118, C119, C134, C135, C137). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with nDSF and inhibition data demonstrating allosteric regulation. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, requesting additional experiments (DUF deletion studies) to distinguish competitive inhibition from allosteric regulation.

Both address the SMALP methodology and purification strategy (C50, C60, C61, C131). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED regarding native-like environment and novelty. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether SMALP truly preserves native lipid environment (suggesting micellar character) and challenging novelty claims as overstated.

Both evaluate the CryoEM structure validation (C91, C92, C93, C94). OpenEval finds the structure SUPPORTED with good agreement to AlphaFold model (RMSD 2.83 Å) at appropriate resolution (~4.1 Å). Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, expressing concern that resolution is significantly below stated 4.1 Å and that the structure is primarily dependent on the AlphaFold model rather than truly validating it.

Both address WbaP dimer formation and oligomerization (C5, C57, C68, C73). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with multiple converging biophysical techniques and crosslinking evidence. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, acknowledging successful isolation of catalytically active dimeric WbaP and novel insights into oligomerization state.

Both address structural homology to dehydratases (C124, C140). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to highly speculative functional implications without experimental validation. Peer reviewers find SUPPORTED, not challenging the structural homology finding and noting conclusions are well-supported by computational data.

Both evaluate AlphaFold dimer prediction (C81, C82, C83). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with high confidence scores and conservation across family members. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, acknowledging validation of AlphaFold model through crosslinking and other biophysical methods.

Both address crosslinking validation of domain swap (C84, C85). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with targeted experiments directly validating AlphaFold predictions. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, acknowledging the crosslinking approach validated the predicted model.

Both address regulatory function assignment (C6, C62). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on nDSF and inhibition data with connection to CpsE studies. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting additional experiments to clarify the regulatory mechanism and distinguish competitive from allosteric inhibition.

Both address structural comparisons to PglC (C106, C107). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED for disorder documentation but notes mechanistic link to substrate specificity remains speculative. Peer reviewers find SUPPORTED, not raising concerns about PglC-WbaP structural comparisons.

Both evaluate structural differences between WbaP and PglC related to substrate specificity (C148, C149). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with well-documented differences in regions important for specificity, though inference remains speculative. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, acknowledging novel insights into WbaP structure without challenging these comparisons.
OpenEval rates comparison to E. coli WbaP as UNCERTAIN (C112, C113) due to unavailable data and ambiguous handedness. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific comparison.

OpenEval rates the proposed conformational change mechanism as UNCERTAIN (C151, C152), noting it is speculative without additional structural states or dynamics data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this mechanistic proposal.

OpenEval rates future application predictions as UNCERTAIN (C129, C130, C158), noting these are predictions rather than demonstrated results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these forward-looking claims.
